  "text": "Ruth was taking the labels off the drawers when her brother arrived.

“You could leave those,” he said.

“The new people won’t want them.”

He set two coffees on the counter. The shop smelled of dust and the orange cleaner their mother had used on everything, including the telephone.

“Which one’s mine?”

“Either. They’re the same.”

Ruth worked a fingernail under BUTTONS—WHITE. The paper came away, leaving a pale rectangle.

“Did the man collect the sewing machines?”

“Yesterday.”

“All six?”

“He counted them twice.”

Her brother opened a drawer. Inside lay a tape measure, curled around a single hook and eye.

“I thought you’d emptied these.”

“I have.”

He held up the tape measure.

“Then that’s yours,” she said.

He pulled out a length. The first few inches had faded almost completely.

“Mum measured my curtains with this.”

“She measured everyone’s curtains.”

“They were too short.”

“You put the rail up afterwards.”

He let the tape fold into his palm.

Through the window, a woman paused beneath the blank space where the sign had been. She looked inside, then continued towards the crossing.

“Shall I turn the lights off?” he asked.

“Not yet.”

Ruth picked up her coffee. It had cooled enough to drink quickly, but she only held it.

Her brother tried another drawer, then closed it carefully.

“What time are we meant to give them the keys?”

“Twelve.”

The clock above the counter said twenty past eleven. Neither of them had changed its battery.

He put the tape measure in his coat pocket.

“Finish your coffee,” he said. “I’ll do the bottom drawers.”"
